text: Rotations vs rebuilding; α-balance; lazy deletion.

Balanced BSTs differ in how they stay balanced. A rotation (旋转) changes the parent–child relation of two nodes while keeping the in-order sequence: rotating x up over its parent y makes y a child of x and hands x's inner subtree to y. Rotating Treaps and Splay trees use rotations; FHQ Treap (第4章) uses split / merge; the scapegoat tree uses complete rebuilding.

Tree Balancing idea Cost Notes Treap (rotating) random priority; rotate up while the heap order is violated expected O(log n) like FHQ, but with rotations FHQ Treap split / merge by random priority expected O(log n) easiest; sequences too (第4章)

Scapegoat tree (替罪羊树) if a subtree is too unbalanced (one side > α of it), flatten and rebuild it perfectly amortised O(log n) no rotations; lazy deletion Splay move every accessed node to the root by rotations amortised O(log n) needed for LCT (第14章) red–black (std::set) colour rules worst O(log n) use the STL

Scapegoat tree: choose α ≈ 0.7. After an insert or delete, walk back up; if some node x has a child subtree larger than α·size(x) (or too many deleted nodes), it is the "scapegoat": collect its subtree in order and rebuild it as a perfectly balanced tree. Deletion only lowers a counter (lazy), so deleted nodes are dropped at the next rebuild.

A rebuild of a subtree of size s costs O(s), but it happens only after Ω(s) updates touched that subtree, so the amortised cost per operation is O(log n). The code is plain recursion with no rotations.

The six operations of P3369 on 60 random operations, checked against a sorted Python list. Predecessor = kth(count of values < x); successor = kth(count of values ≤ x, plus one), using integer values (≤ x is "< x + 1").
Zig-zig and zig-zag; splay after every access.

Splay tree (伸展树): after every access, splay the node to the root with rotations. When x, its parent and grandparent lie in a straight line ("zig-zig") rotate the parent first, then x; when they zig-zag, rotate x twice.
That rule is what gives the amortised O(log n); always rotating x alone does not.

Because the accessed node becomes the root, operations become simple: to delete v, splay it to the root and join its two subtrees; to cut a range [l, r] of a sequence, splay l − 1 to the root and r + 1 below it, and the range is one subtree. LCT (第14章) is built on splay trees.

Same 60 random operations and answers as the scapegoat tree. In remove_, after detaching x the left part is a separate tree, so splaying its maximum p (with fa = 0 as the stop) makes p its root; p has no right child, so the right part hangs there.
Splay every node you walk to (countLess splays the last one visited), otherwise a chain of queries can keep hitting a deep path and the amortised bound is lost.
Alternating medians; boxes; nearest neighbour.

A K-D tree (K-D 树) organises points in k dimensions: the root splits the points by the median x- coordinate, its children by the median y, and so on alternating. Each node also stores the bounding box of its subtree. Building with nth_element is O(n log n).

Nearest neighbour: visit the subtree on the query's side first, and skip any subtree whose bounding box is already farther than the best distance found. Rectangle queries: take whole subtrees whose box is inside, skip boxes outside. Worst case for a 2D rectangle query is O(√n) (简单题 P4148, 天使玩偶 P4169).

With insertions, a K-D tree becomes unbalanced; rebuild it periodically (every √n inserts) or rebuild unbalanced subtrees scapegoat-style. Nearest-neighbour search is fast on random data but can be slow on adversarial inputs.
The Luogu problems for this chapter, a ladder through them, and experiments to try yourself.
Key points to memorise
1. Rotation: x up over its parent; in-order unchanged.
2. Scapegoat: rebuild a subtree when a child > α·size or too many deleted; amortised O(log n).
3. Lazy delete: cnt − 1, drop dead nodes at the next rebuild.
4. Splay: zig-zig rotate parent then x; zig-zag rotate x twice; splay every access.
5. Delete in splay: splay v, join left (max splayed up) and right.
6. K-D tree: alternate split dimensions, store boxes, prune boxes farther than best.
